overview.description: Cross-cutting conventions for component prop APIs, so prop names and shapes are predictable across the whole library instead of decided fresh per component.

rules.name: Use native `disabled`, not `isDisabled`
rules.description: Disabled state must be exposed as the native `disabled` prop/attribute, not a custom `isDisabled` boolean.
rationale: `disabled` is a real HTML attribute: it works with forms, the `:disabled` CSS pseudo-class, and testing-library's toBeDisabled() out of the box.
Re-typing a custom `isDisabled` prop after Omit-ing the native `disabled` attribute is extra code for no behavioral gain.
Checkbox, Switch, and Radio already use `disabled` directly; it is the majority pattern, not the exception.

rules.name: Reserve `is*` prefix for component-owned state
rules.description: The `is*` boolean prop prefix (e.g. isLoading, isFullWidth, isExpanded) should only be used for state that is custom to the component's own visual/behavioral logic — not for anything that maps directly to a native HTML attribute.
rationale: Native attributes (disabled, checked, required, readOnly) already have an established name; renaming them with an `is*` prefix adds a translation layer with no benefit.
Custom component state (loading, full width, expanded) has no native equivalent, so an `is*` prop is the clearest way to name it.

examples: disabled (Checkbox, Switch, Radio, Button, IconButton) — native attribute, not isDisabled

rules.name: `tone` is meaning, `appearance` is visual style
rules.description: A prop that says what a component means (status, intent) is `tone`. A prop that changes how it looks without changing what it means is `appearance` (or `prominence` for the Button family's weight). The two never share a name.
rationale: Separating emphasis from meaning is the reference pattern (Button: `prominence` x `tone`); one name per axis keeps every component readable the same way.
Banner, Section Message, Toast, and Modal Dialog used `appearance` for status until 2026-10-13; they now take `tone`, matching Button, Badge, Label, and Inline Message.

examples: tone (meaning): Button, Badge, Label, Inline Message, Banner, Section Message, Toast, Modal Dialog, Tag, Icon Tile
appearance (style): Link, Icon Tile (default | bold), Skeleton, Progress Indicator

knownViolations: Toggle Button and Toggle Icon Button use `tone` (default | subtle) for visual style; kept by decision on 2026-10-13, and named the same in Figma.

Icon Button, Link Button, and Split Button still take the legacy `appearance` (default | primary | subtle) while Figma has moved them to `tone` + `prominence`; part of the pending Button-family revision.

rules.name: `context` says where a component is shown
rules.description: A component that renders differently inside another one takes `context: 'default' | 'inline'`. `inline` is the chromeless, in-a-row presentation (Figma's `context=inline`).

examples: Field, Text Field, Text Area, Select, Date Picker, Time Picker, Date Time Picker
Field and the pickers pass their context to their control; Table's editable cells force it to inline.

rules.name: One name per value across the system
rules.description: The same idea uses the same value name in every component, in the token names, and in Figma.

examples: Sizes: xxs | xs | sm | md | lg | xl (never small/medium/large/extraLarge)
Light-on-dark: inverse (never inverted); the Button family uses the `isInverse` boolean
Round shapes: round (never circle); square otherwise
The neutral palette: taupe (never gray), the palette's and Figma's name

knownViolations: Alignment mixes physical left | right (Dropdown Menu, Chip Group, Tag Group) with logical start | end (Table, Form) and compound topLeft (Popup). Not yet aligned.

rules.name: Built-in text is a prop
rules.description: Text a component writes itself (an icon-only control's name, a status prefix, a footer label) is a prop with an English default, so it can be translated: `<thing>Label` for a string, `get<Thing>Label` for text built from values.

examples: closeLabel, dismissLabel, clearSearchLabel, previousPageLabel, statusLabel, newTabLabel

knownViolations: Chip names its remove control `removeAriaLabel` where the convention is `removeLabel` (Tag).

rules.name: Renames keep the old name working
rules.description: When a prop or value is renamed, the old one stays accepted as a deprecated alias (typed `@deprecated`, mapped to the new one inside the component), because the LegacyHQ application's code can't be checked from this repo. Remove an alias only after the app has been searched.

examples: Toast and Inline Message accept `info` for `information`
Banner, Section Message, Toast, and Modal Dialog accept `appearance` for `tone`
Text Field, Text Area, and Select accept `appearance` / `tone` (subtle, inline) for `context`
Modal Dialog accepts small/medium/large/extraLarge; Progress Indicator `inverted`; Icon Tile `gray`; Skeleton `circle`

questions: Does this prop correspond to a native HTML attribute?
If yes: use the native name as-is.
If no: is this state genuinely specific to this component's own behavior?
If yes: an `is*`-prefixed boolean is appropriate.
Does this prop say what the component means, or how it looks? Meaning is `tone`; looks are `appearance`.
Does another component already have a name for this value? Use it.
decisionFramework.defaultDecision: Prefer the native attribute name whenever one exists.
decisionFramework.principle: Don't invent a prop name where HTML already has one.
